landing.powerTitle: Covering the main risks in code, runtime, and distribution
landing.powerSub: These protections take effect together after submission and can be tuned in Protection settings.
landing.powerNote: Every protection layer listed above is free of charge.
landing.c1Desc: DEX files are encrypted as a whole so Java / Kotlin code cannot be read after decompilation. Tools such as jadx or apktool return no readable source code or business logic.
landing.c1Scene: Use case: protecting core business logic, endpoint details, and keys.
landing.c2Desc: Critical methods are converted into virtualized instructions instead of standard bytecode, and cannot be restored to their original form after extraction, which substantially raises the cost of reverse engineering.
landing.c2Scene: Use case: core algorithms, payment and license checks, login, and risk control.
landing.c3Desc: Strings inside protected methods are stored encrypted, so endpoints, AppKeys, secrets, and salts appear as plaintext neither in decompiled DEX output nor in decompiled SO output.
landing.c3Scene: Use case: preventing endpoints and keys from being harvested and request rules from being reversed.
landing.c4Desc: Protection against module-injection frameworks such as Xposed: modules cannot attach and hooks do not take effect, so app behavior cannot be altered at runtime by third-party modules.
landing.c4Scene: Use case: preventing ad removal, purchase cracking, and spoofed device data.
landing.c5Desc: Built-in signature consistency checks stop repackaged, re-signed, or code-injected builds from running, which effectively limits the spread of pirated copies.
landing.c5Scene: Use case: preventing repackaged distribution and injected ads or malware.
landing.c6Desc: Frida and other dynamic debugging and hooking tools are detected at runtime; once a debugging environment is found the app can terminate immediately, preventing traffic capture and logic tampering.
landing.c6Scene: Use case: preventing runtime memory analysis, traffic capture, and live logic changes.
landing.sceneTitle: Suitable for all kinds of Android apps
landing.sceneSub: Protection for the typical business scenarios below.
landing.sc1Desc: Account, transaction, and risk-control logic is a primary target for reverse engineering; after hardening no readable business code remains.
landing.sc2Desc: Purchase cracking, ad removal, and modded builds are common; anti-injection plus anti-debugging blocks the usual approaches.
landing.sc3Desc: Internal systems and customer data are sensitive; code encryption reduces the impact of a source-code leak.
landing.sc4Desc: Leaked endpoints, keys, and request rules are quickly abused; after hardening they are no longer exposed in plain form.

landing.cmpTitle: How we compare with other free hardening services
landing.cmpSub: Only services that offer free hardening and open-source hardening projects are covered, with verifiable details where possible and no exaggeration of our own strengths. Third-party names are anonymized.
landing.cmpFeeA: Free personal edition; some features are paid
landing.cmpFeeB: Mainly enterprise-paid, with a free entry point
landing.cmpFeeC: Free basic edition; quotas follow the official terms
landing.cmpVmpB: Supported; more complete in the enterprise edition
landing.cmpVmpC: Limited range on the free edition
landing.cmpStrUs: Supported; no plaintext in DEX or SO
landing.cmpCompatUs: Fine for typical apps; HarmonyOS 6 or later is not supported
landing.cmpServiceUs: Self-service only; no human support or SLA
landing.cmpNote: The comparison covers hardening services that are free or open source. It is based on public information and common hands-on experience; capabilities and pricing are subject to each vendor's official documentation or each project's own docs.
landing.cmpScrollHint: Scroll the table sideways to see the full comparison
landing.cmpGap1: HarmonyOS 6 and later are not supported; do not distribute hardened builds to those versions.
landing.cmpGap2: The wider the VMP extraction scope, the higher the processing time, package size, and runtime overhead; test on real devices.
landing.cmpGap3: As a free platform we are self-service only, with no human support, SLA, or custom hardening plans.
landing.cmpGap4: We do not process an app's existing SO files, and we do not provide iOS hardening or publishing and signing services.
landing.cmpAiText: Some tools advertise one-click "AI hardening" while the actual protection stays at whole-package encryption. The usual problems are listed below; before submitting anything, check the provider's credentials and how it handles your data.
landing.cmpAi1: Poor compatibility: crashes after hardening, failure to launch, or conflicts with third-party SDKs.
landing.cmpAi2: Limited strength: code can be statically restored, and the original logic can often be dumped at runtime.
landing.cmpAi3: Little maintenance: anti-debugging, anti-injection, and signature checks are nominal, and nobody responds when problems appear.
landing.cmpOsTitle: How we compare with open-source hardening projects
landing.cmpWayUs: Non-static: key code is extracted and recompiled into SO
landing.cmpWayB: Free edition is mainly whole-package encryption
landing.cmpWayC: Free edition is mainly whole-package encryption
landing.cmpOsWayA: Function-extraction shell that restores code at runtime
landing.cmpOsCompatUs: Fine for typical apps; test on real devices
landing.safetyText: Uploaded source APKs are used only for this hardening run. They are never repurposed or handed to third parties, and are removed on a regular cleanup schedule.
landing.apiSub: Everything on this page runs through the HTTP endpoints below. The base URL is detected from the domain you are using, and every sample can be copied directly.
landing.apiBaseNote: Hardening endpoints accept POST only. JSON calls use a single envelope format; the upload endpoint uses multipart/form-data. code is 0 on success, otherwise non-zero with a msg.
landing.apiEp1Desc: Checks whether the source APK can be reused and returns today's remaining task quota.
landing.apiEp1Note: When instant_upload is true you can skip the file upload and call upload directly to reuse the source APK.
landing.apiEp2Desc: Submits an APK together with its protection parameters and creates a new hardening task (multipart/form-data).
landing.apiEp2Note: Every call creates an independent task, so the same source APK can be submitted repeatedly with different parameters; instant-upload requests need no file part.
landing.apiEp3Desc: Returns every hardening task for a source APK together with its current status.
landing.apiEp3Note: A null download_url means the result is not ready yet; status 3 means hardening is complete.
landing.apiPFile: The APK file itself; omit it for instant upload
landing.apiPEncryptDex: Encrypt the DEX files: 1 on / 0 off, default 1
landing.apiPEncryptSo: Protect the SO generated by VMP extraction: 1 on / 0 off, default 0
landing.apiPSoLevel: VMP SO protection level: 1 high / 0 low
landing.apiPVmpRules: VMP extraction rules; supports class / extends / implements and wildcards
landing.apiPSignMethod: Signing mode: 0 automatic / 1 use your own signature, default 0
landing.apiPSignature: 64-character certificate SHA-256, required when signing with your own certificate
landing.apiPPassword: Archive password for the result, 1–20 characters, default 123456
landing.apiPMd5List: Array of MD5 values, up to 100 per call; use instead of md5
landing.apiLimitText: Each client IP can create up to 10 hardening tasks per calendar day; instant-upload tasks count as well. A single query call accepts up to 100 MD5 values.
landing.apiErr1001: Invalid parameters, or the endpoint does not exist
landing.apiErr1003: The file is not a valid APK
landing.apiLangText: The page loads its language packs through these endpoints (not part of the hardening API): GET /language/index.php returns the available languages, and GET /language/{file}.json returns one language pack.
landing.apiSecText: Source APKs are used only for this hardening run, are never repurposed or shared, and are removed on a regular cleanup schedule. Results are delivered as an encrypted archive.

landing.faqTitle: Free APK hardening — no sign-up, no login
landing.faqSub: The questions people ask most about cost, registration, data security and compatibility.
landing.faqQ1: Is 星野 Ark really free?
landing.faqA1: Yes, completely. All six protection layers — DEX encryption, code virtualization, string encryption, anti-injection, anti-debugging and signature verification — are free with no paywall. To keep the service stable, each IP can create up to 10 tasks per day.
landing.faqQ2: Do I need to register or log in?
landing.faqA2: No. There is no sign-up and no login, and we do not ask for an email address or phone number — just choose an APK and upload it.
landing.faqQ3: Is my uploaded APK safe? Can it leak?
landing.faqA3: Uploaded APKs are used only for this hardening run, never repurposed or handed to third parties, and removed on a regular cleanup schedule. Results are delivered as an encrypted archive.
landing.faqQ4: What does the hardening actually stop?
landing.faqA4: It prevents DEX files from being read after decompilation, stops key code from being restored, blocks Xposed module injection and Frida debugging, and resists repackaging and re-signing.
landing.faqA5: The default policy fits typical apps and needs no changes. The wider the VMP extraction scope, the higher the processing time and runtime overhead, so test on real devices first. Note that hardened builds do not support HarmonyOS 6 or later.
landing.faqA6: Standard Android APK files. We do not process an app's existing SO files, and iOS hardening or publishing and signing services are not available.
